newsitem.title: UK: RUSSIAN DEBT SURGES TO NEW HIGHS, BRADY BONDS FIRM.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIAN DEBT SURGES TO NEW HIGHS, BRADY BONDS FIRM.

text.p: Russian loans surged to new record highs on Thursday, buoying the wider Brady bond market, as investors took heart from signs Moscow was nearing a deal to restructure its commercial debt.
Dealers reported good demand for Russian debt with dollar-denominated Vneshekonombank loans RUVNUSLNS=RR up a full point at 99-7/8 bid after trading above par for the first time.
"People have woken up this week to the fact that the Russian deal is going to happen and that is what is driving the market," said one dealer.
Russian officials said on Wednesday that the country had reconciled close to 65 percent of its debt to the London Club of commercial bank creditors and an agreement could be closed by the year-end.
Some analysts had expected a higher reconciliation figure at this stage but the fact that the process was continuing on-track was enough to cheer the market.
Some, though, said the market might be running ahead of itself.
"There is a sense of optimism in the market but I think it may be getting a bit carried away," a second dealer said.
"I don't see why people should be buying Vnesh above par when really nothing much has changed. We always assumed there would be a closing before year-end."

Elsewhere, Brazil's Global '27 BRGLB27=RR added 3/8 to 100-5/8 bid, dragged higher by the buoyant Russian market and hopes that the Federal Reserve will not tighten monetary policy this month, allowing emerging debt spreads to tighten further.
Ecuador Discounts ECDISC=RR also gained ground in thin dealings, adding 1/2 to 79-1/2 while Bulgaria IAB BGFLTH11=RR put on 3/8 to 79-5/8.
"The whole Brady market is doing well at the moment. All the indices are at all time highs and it looks like the spreads are going to tighten more," said another dealer.
